metadata.theme: Staying level-headed when a plan falls apart, sharing hard decisions fairly, and asking for help instead of going it alone
metadata.premise: On a wilderness-skills trip above the timberline, a sudden snow slide traps thirteen-year-old Vale Ortiz, two classmates and their guide below a new wall of snow, with the radio crushed and the temperature dropping fast. Vale has to help the group ration gear, treat a bad sprain, and decide whether to wait for rescue or move before dark.

items.name: Bent ski pole
items.description: A sturdy pole, bent but solid. It can test soft snow before you put your weight on it.

clues.name: The crack line
clues.description: A thin, dark line seen in new snow. It can mean the snow below is thin and weak.

passages.title: The Wall of Snow
paragraphs: Vale Ortiz was on a wilderness-skills elective trip with Fernridge Middle School. Vale always noticed small things, even when everyone else was in a hurry.
High above the timberline, the ridge trail cut along the edge of Snowline Hollow.
A loud crack split the quiet air. Snow and rock came down in a sudden, roaring rush.
Grey clouds hung low, like a storm waiting its turn. When the snow finally stopped, a new white wall blocked the old trail home.
Mr. Russo tried to stand and winced hard. He had sprained his ankle in the fall.
Priya's hands shook, and her eyes went wide and worried. Tomas folded his arms and said they should climb straight up and go.

choices.label: Help Mr. Russo with his hurt ankle first
Calm Priya and Tomas before anything else

passages.title: A Careful Splint
paragraphs: Vale knelt down by Mr. Russo in the snow. His ankle was already swelling, puffy and tight.
"It is a sprain, not a break," Vale said, trying hard to sound sure.
Priya passed over the first-aid kit with shaking hands, and Tomas held a flashlight steady.
Vale wrapped the ankle with a splint from the kit, snug but not too tight.
Mr. Russo let out a slow breath. "That is much better," he said. "Thank you, Vale."
There was still the food to sort, and a plan to make before the light got any lower.

choices.label: Wrap it snug, but leave room to move
Wrap it firm so it will not shift

passages.title: Steady Hands
paragraphs: Vale went to Priya first. "We are okay," Vale said. "We just need a plan."
Priya's shoulders dropped a little, and she wiped her eyes on her sleeve.
Tomas still looked ready to charge straight up the new wall of snow alone.
"Let's figure this out together," Vale said. "That way, no one carries it alone."
Mr. Russo's ankle still needed care, and the food still needed to be shared fairly.

choices.label: Stay with Priya a moment longer
Talk Tomas down from climbing alone

passages.title: Sharing What They Had
paragraphs: Four of them, and three days of food between them. Vale laid it all out on a flat rock.
Priya wanted to eat a big meal now, to feel better fast.
Tomas wanted to save almost everything, in case they were stuck a long time.
Vale split the food into small, even shares for each day instead.
Everyone agreed that felt fair. Sharing the choice, not just the food, felt right too.

choices.label: Pack the shares away carefully
Double check the stove and tent too

passages.title: Which Way First
paragraphs: With the ankle wrapped and the food shared, the group looked hard at the new wall of snow.
The radio lay crushed under a rock, in pieces well beyond fixing.
The wall was too tall to climb straight up, and too wide to walk around fast.
Vale could search the scattered gear for anything useful, or scout along the wall for a safer line.
Either way, time was short before the last of the light faded.

choices.label: Search the scattered gear pile
Scout along the new cliff wall

passages.title: The Gear Pile
paragraphs: Snow had made a small mess across the grass near the packs.
A stove, a tent, and the rest of the first-aid kit lay scattered about in the snow.
Under a torn pack flap, Vale spotted a bent ski pole, half buried in frost.
A pole like that could test soft snow before a foot did.
That might stop a bad fall on a hidden slope later on, once they were moving again.

choices.label: Wrap the bent part so it will not slip
Grab the pole fast before the chill gets worse

passages.title: One More Thing
paragraphs: Tucked beside the pole, Vale noticed a torn strip of bright orange cloth.
It must have come loose from a trail marker, ripped free in the slide.
Orange stood out well against the white snow. It might help somebody spot them later.
Vale tucked the cloth into a pocket, just in case, then turned back toward the others.

choices.label: Keep the cloth safe in a pocket
Tie the cloth to the top of the pack

passages.title: The Crack in the Wall
paragraphs: Vale walked along the new wall of snow, looking close at every patch.
A thin, dark line ran across one spot, like a crack through ice.
Below the ridge, hidden by brush, an old deer track crossed the open slope lower down.
It looked small and steep, but it might pass below the worst drop.
A guide had once told Vale that a crack like that meant thin, weak snow underneath.

choices.label: Hurry back to tell the others what you saw
Study the crack a moment longer first

passages.title: One More Thing
paragraphs: On the way back, Vale passed a bent trail marker half covered in snow.
Its bright paint still showed through the white.
Vale remembered which way the marker had pointed, back toward the old main trail.
That small fact might matter later, once they were moving again.

choices.label: Remember the marker's direction clearly
Hurry on before losing the light

passages.title: Regroup at the Wall
paragraphs: Vale came back to the others at the flat rock.
Priya paced in a small, tight circle, and Tomas sat with his arms crossed on the ground.
Mr. Russo's splint held steady, and the food was packed fair and square.
There was still a little time before dark, but not much of it left.
Something else might still be worth checking before they moved on for good.

choices.label: Go back and check the gear pile too
choices.lockedHint: You already checked the gear pile.

choices.label: Go back and scout the cliff wall too
choices.lockedHint: You already scouted the cliff wall.

choices.label: Decide together to head for the ridge gap

passages.title: A Second Look
paragraphs: Vale jogged back toward the gear, where snow still made a small mess across the grass.
Near a torn pack flap, half buried in frost, sat a bent ski pole.
Vale picked it up fast. It could test soft snow before anyone took a bad fall.
A bad slip on a hidden slope was a risk nobody wanted to take.

choices.label: Wrap the bent part before it slips
Grab it fast before the chill gets worse

passages.title: A Second Look at the Wall
paragraphs: Vale jogged to the new wall of snow for one more look.
The thin, dark crack line still ran across the same patch.
Below the ridge, the old deer track still crossed the open slope lower down.
It looked small and steep, but it might pass below the worst drop.

choices.label: Fix the crack's spot firmly in mind
Hurry back before the chill gets worse

passages.title: Toward the Gap
paragraphs: The group moved together along the base of the new snow wall.
Priya wanted to hurry on ahead, since she was fast on her feet.
Tomas matched his pace to Mr. Russo's slow, careful steps instead.
Little by little, the light over the ridge turned a deeper grey.

choices.label: Let Priya range a little ahead to look
Keep everyone close together at Mr. Russo's pace

passages.title: The Ridge Gap
paragraphs: The group reached a narrow gap in the new wall of snow.
Beyond it, the old deer track curved around the open slope.
Crossing the gap looked fast, but the snow near the edge looked soft.
Waiting here and raising a bright signal was slower, but safer if the gap was too risky.

choices.label: Test the soft snow with the pole and cross
choices.lockedHint: You need the ski pole and the memory of the crack line to risk the gap.

choices.label: Stay put and raise a bright signal instead

passages.title: Across the Gap
paragraphs: Vale pressed the pole into the snow before every step.
The crack line showed exactly where the crust turned thin and weak.
One by one, the group crossed the narrow gap and found the old deer track.
The track led to a small ranger shelter tucked under a rock overhang.
Daylight was fading fast now, and a choice still waited for them.

choices.label: Check on Mr. Russo before anything else
Scan the ridge for any sign of rescue first

passages.title: The Last Hour of Light
paragraphs: Inside the shelter, out of the wind, the group looked at each other.
There was still time to choose, but not much time left to waste.
Mr. Russo's ankle needed care. The failing light needed a plan. The whole team needed a fair choice.

choices.label: Splint the ankle well and keep moving together
Build a bright signal on open ground and wait
Let Tomas push ahead alone for faster help
Split into two small teams to rig a sled

passages.title: Down Together
paragraphs: Vale and Priya wrapped Mr. Russo's ankle tight with a fresh splint from the kit.
He gripped Tomas's arm, and together the four of them stood him up.
Step by step, the group moved down the old deer track. No one wanted to spill the last of their strength too soon.
Past the shelter, a bright patch of orange showed through the snow: a search team's flag.
The searchers had heard about the missed check-in from the wilderness class and had already started looking.
Everyone made it down together, cold but steady. Small details, and asking for help, had made the hard day easier.

passages.title: Seen From Above
paragraphs: The group laid out every bright thing they owned in a big X shape on the open snow.
Priya and Tomas took turns to climb a low rock and watch the sky.
After a cold hour, a small plane dipped low and tipped its wings at them.
The search had begun the moment their wilderness class failed to cross the usual checkpoint.
Rescuers followed the bright signal and reached the shelter well before full dark.
Waiting together, calm and ready, had worked out just fine in the end.

passages.title: Faster Alone
paragraphs: Tomas set off alone down the old deer track, moving fast over the packed snow.
He crossed the last ridge and found a small ranger station by dusk.
Rescuers climbed back up his tracks to find the others, tired but safe.
Tomas felt proud. But later he said the hardest part was not knowing if the others were okay.
Vale agreed that next time, the group should decide together, even when someone feels ready to run ahead.

passages.title: Working As One
paragraphs: One team rigged a makeshift sled from a tent and poles, strapping Mr. Russo in gently.
The other team went ahead to track a safe line through a drift of soft snow.
No one made a wrong step, and no one took a bad fall on the way down.
By the time the last small patch of daylight faded, both teams met rescuers at the trail's end.
Splitting the work fairly had let them move fast and still stay safe.

passages.title: A Cold, Safe Wait
paragraphs: The group chose to stay by the wall and wait it out.
They raised a bright flag and huddled close together against the chill.
Hours passed slowly. Snow kept drifting against their boots, and the cold crept in close.
No one tried the gap without the right gear, so no one took a bad fall.
Long after dark, a search team found their trail and reached them, cold but unhurt.
Next time, Vale thought, the right gear might get them home before the chill set in. For now, waiting together had kept everyone safe.

wilderness.definition: Wild, natural land away from towns and roads.

elective.definition: A class or trip you choose to take, not one you must take.

together.definition: All in the same place, doing something as a group.

overhang.definition: A ledge of rock or snow that sticks out above, like a roof.

timberline.definition: The high point on a mountain where trees stop growing.

radio.definition: A device used to send and hear voices over a distance.

rescuers.definition: People who come to help and bring others to safety.

sprain.definition: A twist that hurts a joint, without breaking a bone.

splint.definition: A stiff support that holds a hurt joint still.

signal.definition: A sign, like a light or flag, that shows people where you are.

shelter.definition: A safe place that blocks wind, snow or rain.

checkpoint.definition: A place where someone is expected to check in or be seen.
